content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"FULL","rationale":"The entry's core identification — dew as the word of God descending silently from heaven — is carried directly by Deuteronomy 32:2, which explicitly equates 'my speech' with distilling dew, and is reinforced by the printed manna chain: the manna falls upon the dew (Num 11:9), is revealed when the dew lifts (Ex 16:14), and is expressly decoded by Moses himself as teaching that man lives 'by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD' (Deut 8:3). 1 Kings 17:1 further binds dew to 'my word.' The strongest counter — the common reading that dew primarily symbolizes divine blessing/favor — does not contradict the core, since even the common-interpretation responses list 'God's word or teaching' as a recognized sense grounded in the very verse the entry leads with; more importantly, the blessing label cannot explain the explicit speech-equals-dew equation of Deut 32:2 or the deliberate dew-manna-word mechanic of Ex 16/Num 11/Deut 8:3 as well as the entry does. The closing elaboration ('received without root, it evaporates when the sun grows hot') is supported by the same passage's continuation (the manna melted when the sun waxed hot, Ex 16:21), by Hosea 14:5's pairing of dew with cast-forth roots, and by the sower framework the book has already established (seed=word from Deut 32:2 and Isa 55:10-11; the rootless hearer withering under the sun). No supplied text is better explained by the blessing reading than by the word reading.","book_core_identification":"Dew symbolizes the word of God descending from heaven — arriving silently and nightly, found in the morning — per Deut 32:2's explicit 'my speech shall distil as the dew.'","book_secondary_elaborations":["The manna falls upon the dew, and when the dew lifts the word lies on the ground as daily bread (Num 11:9; Ex 16:14; Deut 8:3 identifying manna with 'every word' from the LORD's mouth).","The word so received, if it takes no root, evaporates when the sun grows hot (echoing Ex 16:21's manna melting in the hot sun, Hos 14:5's dew-with-roots imagery, and the rootless hearer of the sower parable)."],"unsupported_glossary_assertions":[],"chapter_only_objections":["The cross-referenced chapter (The Pearls of Wisdom, ch. 31) is primarily about the pearl, the moon, and the bride; its treatment of dew is incidental (Prov 3:20; Deut 33:13-14), so most direct support for the entry actually comes from the sower-chapter method excerpt rather than ch. 31.","The chapter's lunar-calendar claims (keseh/kisse wordplay, full-moon month-start, east-gate typology) are speculative and unproven, but none of them are asserted in the glossary entry.","The chapter's identification of the pearl as the full moon and the bride is a separate symbolic claim not under judgment here."],"strongest_counter_interpretation":"Dew primarily symbolizes divine blessing, favor, and life-giving grace (Gen 27:28; Deut 33:13, 28; Hos 14:5; Ps 133:3; Mic 5:7; Zech 8:12), with the word/teaching sense of Deut 32:2 treated as a secondary use and the transience motif of Hos 6:4 as another distinct use.","counter_core_identification":"Dew is God's quiet, life-giving blessing and favor descending on His people, tied to fertility and provision; its withholding signals judgment.","counter_relation_to_book_core":"SAME_CORE_BROADER","material_core_denial":"The counter does not deny that Deut 32:2 figures God's speech as dew; it only demotes that sense to a secondary use beneath a broader 'blessing' label. Since a broader label that concedes the word-sense does not make both core identifications incompatible for the same referent, there is no material core denial.","counter_case":["The largest cluster of dew texts (Gen 27:28; Deut 33:13, 28; Ps 133:3; Mic 5:7; Zech 8:12; Prov 19:12) concerns agricultural blessing and favor, not speech.","Hos 14:5 in the entry's own reference list reads naturally as restorative blessing ('I will be as the dew unto Israel: he shall grow as the lily').","1 Kgs 17:1 can be read simply as withheld blessing/judgment rather than a dew-word linkage.","Standard commentaries and Bible dictionaries treat blessing/grace as the leading sense, with the doctrine sense as a recognized but secondary use."],"book_explanatory_advantages":["Deut 32:2 is the one text where Scripture itself states the equation — 'my speech shall distil as the dew' — an explicit self-decoding key of exactly the kind the book's method (Isa 5:7; 2 Sam 12:7) privileges; the blessing reading has no comparably explicit defining verse.","Only the word reading explains the dew-manna mechanic as a unit: dew descends nightly, the manna lies upon it when it lifts (Num 11:9; Ex 16:14), and Deut 8:3 explicitly interprets the manna as 'every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD' — daily bread as daily word.","1 Kgs 17:1 ties dew's presence or absence directly to 'my word,' cohering with the entry's identification.","The evaporation clause explains Ex 16:21 (manna melting when the sun waxed hot) and the rootless-hearer pattern in one figure, using Hos 14:5's root imagery as the positive counterpart.","The reading coheres with the already-demonstrated rain/seed=word pattern (Isa 55:10-11; Deut 32:2) from the sower derivation, giving multi-witness support across Moses, the Prophets, and the Writings."],"counter_explanatory_advantages":["The blessing reading covers the widest set of dew passages across Scripture (Gen 27:28; Deut 33; Ps 133:3; Mic 5:7; Zech 8:12), most of which the entry's curated references do not include.","It aligns with the recognized consensus of commentators and Bible dictionaries.","It handles Hos 14:5 with no interpretive step at all."],"evidence_book_core_cannot_explain":[],"comparative_winner":"BOOK","decisive_sources":["Deuteronomy 32:2 — the explicit equation of God's speech with distilling dew","Deuteronomy 8:3 with Numbers 11:9 and Exodus 16:14 — the dew-manna-word chain identifying the morning bread as the word","1 Kings 17:1 — dew given or withheld 'according to my word'","Hosea 14:5 — dew producing rooted growth, supplying the positive counterpart to rootless evaporation"],"unresolved_objections":["The entry's curated reference list omits the large blessing-cluster texts (Gen 27:28; Deut 33; Ps 133:3), so the glossary sense is established for the entry's chosen passages rather than shown to be the dominant sense of dew across all of Scripture; the entry, however, defines a symbolic sense rather than claiming exclusivity, so this does not defeat it.","The 'sun grows hot' evaporation detail rests on Ex 16:21 and the sower parable, neither of which is printed among the entry's references, though both are squarely within the cited passages' immediate context and the book's established method."],"confidence":"high"}
